title: fix(console): the boot preflight get-session carries the cookie so a renewed session cookie is stored (objectui#12892)
body:
Fixes #12892
Clause-②: no

## What changed

`apps/console/src/lib/auth-preflight.ts`: the pre-React preflight's `GET .../get-session` now sends `credentials: 'include'` instead of `'omit'`. It still sends `Authorization: Bearer TOKEN` and `Accept: application/json`. The file's header comment now gives the new reason, in a section called "Why the cookie rides along (objectui#12892)". The paragraph on the hand-off now says the request carries the same Bearer and the same cookie. Past `updateAge` this read renews the session row and re-issues the cookie. An `omit` fetch never stores a response cookie, so the row outlived the cookie. Since objectui#12808 this read is the boot's only session read, so it has to be the one that stores the cookie. That follows the framework rule in objectstack `packages/spec/src/contracts/auth-service.ts` (the objectstack-ai/objectstack#22384 note): a browser session renews only on the `get-session` route, which re-issues the cookie. Route (2) from triage `6235408974`. `packages/auth/src/createAuthClient.ts` is not touched: `takePreflightSession` compares the auth URL and the token, and neither depends on the cookie.

## Why the stale-token check is unchanged (A1, measured)

- **How the preflight decides "stale" (unchanged by this diff):** `res.ok` and a `user` in the body (`body.user` or `body.data.user`) mean valid. Any other answer (401, other 4xx, or 200 with null) means stale: the token and every active-org key are purged. A network error keeps the token.
- **The server judges by the Bearer when both are present.** better-auth 1.7.2's `bearer()` plugin (`dist/plugins/bearer/index.mjs`, the `before` hook) calls `setRequestCookie(headers, sessionToken.name, decodedToken)`. This writes the Bearer's token over the session cookie the request carried. So a stale Bearer beside a live cookie still answers null. The framework pins the same precedence: objectstack `packages/plugins/plugin-auth/src/two-factor-rotated-token-echo.test.ts`, test "a bogus bearer still overrides a valid cookie and still fails loud". `bearer()` is always enabled in `auth-manager.ts`.
- **Boundary (not modelled by a test here):** `bearer()` skips a dotted token whose HMAC signature does not verify. A request carrying such a token is judged by its cookie. That happens only when the signing secret has changed, and then the cookie, which was signed with the same old secret, fails too. Under `omit` that request answered null. Under `include` it answers whatever the cookie answers, which is the same answer every later request with that header gets. I found no other path where adding the cookie changes the answer.
- **Cross-origin:** `include` needs the credentialed-CORS headers. AuthProvider's own better-auth client already sends `include`. If those headers are missing, the preflight's fetch rejects, it takes the existing "network error, keep the token" branch, and AuthProvider asks the server itself.

## Tests

New file: `apps/console/src/__tests__/authPreflightCredentials-12892.test.ts`, next to `sessionBootDedup.test.tsx`. It stubs `fetch` with `vi.stubGlobal` and uses no `vi.mock`.

- (a) The request is `GET AUTH_URL/get-session` with `credentials: 'include'`, `Authorization: Bearer tok_live` and `Accept: application/json`.
- (b) A stale Bearer beside a live cookie is still judged stale. The stub server models one fact: the Bearer is read first, and the cookie only when no Bearer is sent. Its jar holds a LIVE session, which is sent only when `credentials === 'include'`. The test first checks that the model's cookie answers a session when no Bearer is sent, so the null comes from the Bearer and not from an empty jar. Then the real preflight purges the token and the active-org key and hands nothing on. The stub does not model the browser storing `Set-Cookie`. That part comes from the Fetch spec and from the card's Chromium probe (`omit` not stored, `include` stored).
- (c) CONTROL: with no stored token, nothing is sent, nothing is purged and nothing is handed on.

**Ablation** (with `/home/user/objectstack/scripts/ablation-replace.mjs`, run on the committed fix; this test imports the source by relative path, so no build was needed):
- Anchor `credentials: 'include',` → `credentials: 'omit',`, 1 hit → 0. Blob `0de919a3e37f` → `ebeb16519299`.
- Result: (a) and (b) went red with `expected 'omit' to be 'include'`. Summary: `Tests  2 failed | 1 passed (3)`. The control (c) stayed green.
- Restore: blob after restore `0de919a3e37f` equals the HEAD blob, and `git diff HEAD` is empty.
- (b)'s purge half alone would not fail under `omit`, because no cookie is sent then. (b) pins the purge WITH the cookie present. The request shape is held by (a) and by (b)'s first assertion.

## Acceptance notes

- Still open: the card's end-to-end reading (in objectstack-ai/cloud#2699, the time the session row outlives the cookie after a boot past `updateAge` should read 0 s). That is cloud's to read once its `.objectui-sha` includes this change. The unit pins hold the request shape and the stale-token judgment, not a real browser's cookie jar.
